items.titleZh: 汉密尔顿与勒克莱尔在法拉利的领袖之争
items.summaryZh: The Race回顾汉密尔顿与勒克莱尔在法拉利争夺车队核心地位的碰撞过程，墨西哥站的最新摩擦表明2026赛季重新打开了这一话题，但两人都尚未决定性地占据主动。
items.originalTitle: How the collision course between Hamilton and Leclerc was created
items.summaryEn: The Race reviews how the collision course between Hamilton and Leclerc at Ferrari took shape, noting that their latest fracas in Mexico showed 2026 has reopened the debate over who leads the team without either driver decisively seizing the initiative.
detailZh: 上赛季结束时，刘易斯·汉密尔顿在马拉内罗艰难的第一年，似乎已经回答了谁是法拉利在F1的领军人物这一问题。
汉密尔顿与夏尔·勒克莱尔在墨西哥的最新摩擦表明，2026赛季不仅重新打开了这一争论，而且尚未让其中一位车手决定性地占据主动。
F1车手就是这样成为事实上的领袖的。忘掉合同怎么写，也忘掉领队看似给予的恩宠与偏爱，如果你是更强的车手，车队就会围绕你凝聚。
这正是勒克莱尔和汉密尔顿决心抓住每个机会证明自己的原因。而这一局面需要车库两侧的形势发生明显变化才会形成。
第一个问题是勒克莱尔最初对2026年规格赛车感到挣扎。虽然年初有一段时间，制动问题放大了这一困境，但那是暂时的。
然而，他经常批评那些不奖励他风格的赛车，因为需要在动力单元部署和能量回收方面进行一定程度的工程优化以保持一致性。这导致他不得不以不那么直觉的方式驾驶。
“这些赛车迫使我们做职业生涯中从未做过的事情，”勒克莱尔说。
“车手的多面性始终是好事，因为在职业生涯中你必须驾驶不同的赛车，从而为你的驾驶增添工具，并能够应对每一种情况。
“而今年，尤其是比任何其他年份都更明显，我们驾驶的方式非常奇怪。”
“有时候这并不是我特别喜欢的事情，但我认为作为一名车手，从长远来看这会是有益的。”
勒克莱尔是适应上一代赛车要求最快的车手之一，尤其是在调整刹车风格方面，当时队友卡洛斯·塞恩斯花了更长得多的时间才掌握，但这一次他却遇到了困难。
然而，正如车队领队弗雷德·瓦塞尔所指出的，勒克莱尔在本赛季取得了显著进步。
瓦塞尔表示：“也许确实如此，在他的驾驶风格中，他习惯于在Q3多做一次额外推进，而在这些规则下，这并不总能奏效。”
“他在理解规则、赛车、如何跑得更快、如何调校赛车方面恢复得很好。
“这并不容易，因为我认为挑战是巨大的。在赛季初进行重置，当你过去20年一直以某种方式驾驶，说要稍微早一点踩油门，而我们现在说‘不，不再是那样了，现在你必须一次性踩下去’……
“我不想说这不是同一项运动，但方式不同了。这对每个人都是如此，我认为有时我们低估了他们面临的挑战。但在那段困难时期之后，他恢复得很好。”
在勒克莱尔经历这一过程的同时——需要指出的是，尽管他目前状态良好，但尚未达到自己的绝对最佳水平——汉密尔顿也取得了进步。
2025年，他对法拉利缺乏熟悉度，这让他举步维艰，并公开质疑自己的能力，但第二年则完全不同。这是造成当前局面的第二个因素。
“对刘易斯来说这很艰难——用这个词来形容可能都算轻描淡写了，”瓦塞尔在谈到汉密尔顿面临的挑战时说道。
“这很艰难，因为这是在迈凯伦-梅赛德斯以及随后梅赛德斯共20年之后（发生的）。我个人低估了这一跨越的难度。
并不是说我们做得更差或更好，而是我们只是做得不一样。这不仅仅是食物或天气的问题，每一个软件都不同，每一个部件都不同，他身边的人也不同。
如果你没有掌控好一切，你就会在桌上留下零点几秒的差距。
而在我们25年所拥有的竞争格局下——我记得是阿布扎比Q1，从P5到P15之间只差十分之一秒[勒克莱尔P5与汉密尔顿P16之间为0.231秒，编者注]——这意味着我们并未完全掌控赛车套件的每一个细节，我们也稍微偏离了赛季的轨迹。
我记得布达佩斯，查尔斯在Q2比刘易斯快十分之一秒，但刘易斯是P11[实际差距为0.247秒，编者注]，而最终查尔斯拿下了杆位。
这不是借口，也不是一个好理由，你必须排在所有人前面，但归根结底，我们谈论的是细节，我认为我们或许低估了文化的改变、他身边人员的改变、一切的改变。
汉密尔顿仍在上升，期待他在下赛季取得进一步收获是合理的。和勒克莱尔一样，他表现出色，但也知道还有更多潜力可挖，这应该会让他在2027年再次变得更强一些。
这两条轨迹已经形成了一条碰撞路线，尽管车队里所有人都会希望它不会从比喻变成现实。
这关乎两名车手，他们都在不断打磨在这支车队和这些赛车中达到最佳状态所需的一切，同时决心通过纯粹的表现让自己成为车队的焦点。
这对车队来说有时可能会分散注意力，甚至适得其反，但从旁观者的角度看却令人兴奋。而根据目前的证据，这场争斗可能会一直持续到2027年。
detailEn: At the end of last season, the question of who was Ferrari’s spearhead in Formula 1 had seemingly been answered by Lewis Hamilton’s difficult first year at Maranello.
The latest fracas between Hamilton and Charles Leclerc in Mexico underlined that 2026 not only reopened the debate, but hasn’t yet led to one driver or the other decisively seizing the initiative.
This is how F1 drivers become the de facto leader. Forget what contracts say or the perceived grace and favour of a team boss, if you are the stronger driver the team will coalesce around you.

That’s exactly why Leclerc and Hamilton are determined to assert themselves at every opportunity. And it required a significant shift of the landscape on both sides of the garage to create this scenario.
The first was Leclerc initially struggling with the 2026-spec cars. While there was a stretch early in the year when this was exaggerated by braking troubles, that was temporary.

However, he’s regularly criticised cars that don’t reward his style given the need to engineer in a level of consistency to optimise the power unit deployment and harvesting. That’s led to him having to drive in a less intuitive way.
"These cars are making us do things that we've never done before in our career," says Leclerc.
"Versatility of the driver is always a good thing because in a career you've got to drive different cars in order to kind of add tools to your driving and being able to manage every situation.
"And this year, particularly more than any other year, we are driving in ways that are very strange.
"Sometimes it's not something that I particularly enjoy, but I think as a driver, it will be beneficial in the long term."

Whereas Leclerc was one of the fastest to adapt to the demands of the last generation of cars, particularly in modifying his braking style in a way it took then-team-mate Carlos Sainz far longer to master, this time he has struggled.
However, as team boss Fred Vasseur points out, Leclerc has made significant gains through this season.
"It’s true perhaps that [in] his driving style he was used to doing an extra push in Q3, and this does not always pay off with these regulations," says Vasseur.
"He had a good recovery in understanding of the regulations, the car, how to be faster, how to set-up the car.

“It was not easy, because I think the challenge is huge. To do the reset at the beginning of the season when you spent the last 20 years [driving a certain way], saying you have to go on the throttle a bit earlier and we say ‘no, it’s not like this anymore, now you have to go on [it in] one shot’...

"I don’t want to say it’s not the same sport, but the approach is different. This is true for everybody and I think that sometimes we underestimate the challenge for them. But after this difficult period, he had a good recovery."
While Leclerc has been working through this process - and it’s important to note that while he is operating at a good level he is still not at his absolute best - Hamilton has also made strides.
In 2025, his lack of familiarity with Ferrari meant he struggled and publicly doubted his own ability, but year two has been completely different. This is the second factor creating this situation.
"It was difficult for Lewis - and that’s a small word [for it] probably," says Vasseur of the challenge Hamilton faced.
"It was difficult because [it came] after 20 years with McLaren-Mercedes and then Mercedes. I personally underestimated the step.

"It's not that we are doing worse or better, it’s that we are just doing differently. It's not just about the food or weather, every single [piece of] software is different, every single component is different, the people around him are different.
"And if you are not on top of everything, you leave on the table a couple of hundredths of seconds.

And with the field that we had in '25 - I think it was Abu Dhabi Q1 that you had one tenth between P5 and P15 [it was 0.231s between Leclerc in P5 and Hamilton in P16, ed] - it meant that we were not in the full control of every single detail of the package, and we lost a little bit the path of the season.
"I have in mind Budapest when Charles in Q2 was one-tenth faster than Lewis but Lewis was P11 [the gap was actually 0.247s, ed], and at the end Charles finished with pole position.

"It's not an excuse, it's not a good reason, you have to be in front of everybody, but at the end of the day, we are speaking about details and I think perhaps we underestimate the change of culture, the change of people around him, the change of everything."

Hamilton is still on the up and it’s reasonable to expect further gains next season. Like Leclerc, he’s performing well but knows there’s more to come, which should make him a little stronger again in 2027.
These two trajectories have created a collision course, albeit one that everyone in the team will hope doesn’t make the transition from metaphor to reality.

It’s about two drivers, both still chipping away at what it takes to be at their best in this team and in these cars while determined to make themselves the focal point of the team through outright performance.

It might be distracting and even counter-productive at times for the team, but it’s thrilling to watch from the outside. And based on the current evidence, this is a fight that could rage on into 2027.
keyPointsZh: 文章认为，决定谁是车队实际领袖的不是合同或领队的偏爱，而是更强的车手会让车队围绕自己凝聚。
勒克莱尔和汉密尔顿因此都决心抓住每个机会证明自己，这一局面需要车库两侧形势发生明显变化才会形成。
keyPointsEn: The article argues that de facto team leadership is not decided by contracts or a team boss's favour, but by the stronger driver around whom the team coalesces.
That is why Leclerc and Hamilton are determined to assert themselves at every opportunity, a scenario that required a significant shift of the landscape on both sides of the garage.

items.titleZh: 马克·休斯：艾伦·琼斯令对手胆寒，是威廉姆斯的完美人选
items.summaryZh: 艾伦·琼斯去世，享年80岁。他以强悍、心理坚韧和极具侵略性的轮对轮驾驶风格，成为弗兰克·威廉姆斯和帕特里克·海德打造威廉姆斯车队的理想车手，并共同赢得1980年车手和车队世界冠军。
items.originalTitle: Mark Hughes: Alan Jones terrified rivals and was perfect for Williams
items.summaryEn: Alan Jones has died at the age of 80. Known for his strength, mental toughness and aggressive wheel-to-wheel racing, he became the ideal driver for Frank Williams and Patrick Head as they built up the Williams team, and together they won the 1980 drivers' and constructors' world titles.
detailZh: 强壮如牛，心理素质比任何坐进赛车的人都要坚韧，是最具侵略性的轮对轮车手，把对手吓得魂飞魄散。
难怪艾伦·琼斯——他已去世，享年80岁——会成为弗兰克·威廉姆斯和帕特里克·海德心目中完美车手的原型，两人携手让威廉姆斯车队从无到有地崭露头角。他们一起赢得1980年车手和车队世界冠军，正式确立了这一地位。
1970年，他怀揣50英镑从澳大利亚来到英国参加F3时，并没有被特别看好会成为世界冠军。
但他在动力不足的方程式赛车中是个壮实的家伙，却仍在英国F3和Formula Atlantic中连续几个赛季位居前列。
他第一次获得F1机会是在1975年，加入了格雷厄姆·希尔的团队，随后又为哈里·斯蒂勒的私人赫斯基思车队效力。
他的表现足以让约翰·苏尔特斯在76赛季签下他。在非锦标赛的冠军赛上，他领跑并与詹姆斯·亨特的迈凯伦赛车缠斗，预示了他后来的状态，但那个赛季并不高调，琼斯和苏尔特斯这两个固执的人对各自的处境都不满意，因此相处得并不融洽。赛季结束后琼斯离开了，他宁愿退出F1也不愿留在那种环境中。
这使得他在77赛季开始四场比赛后有空档，在汤姆·普赖斯于南非大奖赛致命事故后，他作为临时替补加入了影子车队。
影子DN8赛车有点超重，但平衡性足够好，让琼斯的天赋得以显现。他在雨中的奥地利大奖赛上获胜，多少有些出人意料，但整个赛季他都很快、稳定且富有战斗力。
弗兰克·威廉姆斯签下他加入自己1978年的单赛车车队，理由是“一个能稳定为我们拿分的人，但我们很快意识到，我们碰上的东西比那要好得多”。
那一年有好几场让巨头胆寒的表现，那是1979年下半年一连串胜利的前奏。从那时起，琼斯和威廉姆斯合在一起就是F1的黄金标准，贯穿他们1980年的夺冠赛季，甚至在被可靠性问题困扰的1981年也是如此。琼斯和地面效应威廉姆斯FW07是天作之合。
在1981赛季收官战拉斯维加斯大奖赛上碾压对手后，他第一次退役。他被说服在1985-86赛季全职回归，但纽曼-哈斯项目未能兑现其潜力，琼斯随后第二次退役。
表面上礼貌而端正，但头盔一戴上，琼斯就让对手胆寒。
他谁也不怕，非常擅长识别自己需要赛车提供什么才能跑得更快，然后就会把那辆车开到轮子都快飞了。正因如此，他在威廉姆斯车队被奉若神明，即便在他离开之后，车队也很大程度上继承了他的性格。
detailEn: Strong like an ox, psychologically more airtight than anyone who's ever climbed into a race car, and the most aggressive wheel-to-wheel racer who scared the living daylights out of his rivals.

Little wonder Alan Jones - who has died, aged 80 - became an archetype of the perfect racing driver for Frank Williams and Patrick Head as they jointly put the Williams team on the map out of nowhere. It was a status they formalised by winning the 1980 drivers' and constructors' world titles together.
He wasn't particularly rated as an obvious world champion when he come over to the UK from Australia with £50 in his back pocket, to race in F3 in 1970.
But he was a hefty guy in an under-powered formula and still he was a frontrunner for a few seasons in British F3 and Formula Atlantic.
His first F1 chance came in 1975, with Graham Hill's team and a subsequent ride in Harry Stiller's privateer Hesketh.

He showed enough for John Surtees to take him on for the '76 season. At the non-championship Race of Champions he foreshadowed his later form by leading and dicing with James Hunt's McLaren but it was a low-key season and Jones and Surtees, as two hard-headed individuals dissatisfied with their situation, didn't hit it off. Jones left at the end of the season, prepared to walk out of F1 rather than stay in that environment.
Which made him available four races into the '77 season as a short-notice replacement at Shadow after Tom Pryce's fatal accident in the South African Grand Prix.

The Shadow DN8 was a little overweight but well-balanced enough for Jones' talent to become apparent. His victory in the wet Austrian Grand Prix was something of a shock result but he was quick, consistent and combative all year.
Frank Williams signed him for his single-car '78 team on the basis of "someone who could score us points regularly but we quickly realised we'd stumbled onto something rather better than that".

There were several giant-scaring performances that year, the prelude to a whole stream of victories in the latter half of '79. In combination, Jones and Williams were F1's gold standard from there, through their title 1980 season and even in their reliability-blighted '81. Jones and the ground effect Williams FW07 were made for each other.

He retired for the first time after trouncing the opposition in the season-ending '81 Las Vegas Grand Prix. He was persuaded back full time for '85-86 but the Newman Haas project didn't live up to its potential and Jones' second retirement duly followed.
Superficially polite and correct, Jones terrified his rivals when the helmet went on.

He was afraid of no one, was brilliantly adept at identifying what he needed from a car to go faster and he'd then race the wheels off it. For that he was deified at Williams and the team took on much of his character even after he'd left.
keyPointsZh: 1970年，他怀揣50英镑从澳大利亚前往英国参加F3。
他驾驶动力不足的赛车，仍在英国F3和Formula Atlantic中连续几个赛季位居前列。
keyPointsEn: In 1970 he came to the UK from Australia with £50 to race in F3.
Despite driving under-powered cars, he was a frontrunner for several seasons in British F3 and Formula Atlantic.

items.originalTitle: 1980 F1 world champion Alan Jones dies aged 80
detailZh: 1980年F1世界冠军艾伦·琼斯逝世享年80岁
澳大利亚1980年一级方程式世界冠军艾伦·琼斯因短期疾病逝世，享年80岁，留下了包括12场大奖赛胜利和威廉姆斯车队首个车手总冠军在内的辉煌成就
1980年世界车手冠军、澳大利亚的艾伦·琼斯周四在黄金海岸逝世
琼斯家人发表声明称，他因短期疾病去世。享年80岁。
“我们非常悲痛地宣布，我们深爱的艾伦于11月5日因短期疾病去世，”巴特勒-戴维斯说。
他将被与他最亲近的人以及一直支持他的众多粉丝深深怀念。
艾伦将一生奉献给赛车运动，他留下的遗产将通过他沿途所触及的无数人继续传承。
通过他在赛道上和赛道下的成就、激情和无可置疑的性格，艾伦在国内外体育界留下了持久的印记。
“作为一个家庭，我们想借此机会感谢所有参与艾伦旅程多年友谊、爱和支持的人。他非常幸运，身边有这么多美好的人。”
琼斯于1946年出生于墨尔本，是商人兼赛车手斯坦·琼斯的儿子，在父亲在1959年朗福德澳大利亚大奖赛获胜时，他在场边观看。年轻的琼斯在1980年卡尔德公园重复了这一壮举，成为最后一位赢得这场比赛的澳大利亚车手，这场比赛被认为是世界上第二古老的Grand Prix。
琼斯在20世纪60年代在英国赛车界小试牛刀后回到澳大利亚，然后在1970年搬到伦敦。他花了三年时间才确立自己的地位，1973年在银石赢得了他的第一个Formula 3赛事，同年他在GRD赛车中获得了英国F3锦标赛的亚军。
弗兰克·德尼、弗兰克·威廉姆斯和艾伦·琼斯
1975年，他在西班牙大奖赛上驾驶Hesketh赛车首次亮相一级方程式赛车，在那个赛季结束后，他转投Graham Hill的团队，后来又加入了Surtees车队。
那个车队也即将关闭，Jones的职业生涯似乎陷入了停滞——直到Shadow车队在南非失去了领队车手Tom Pryce后，向他伸出了橄榄枝。在一段童话般的结果中，Jones在奥地利赛道上，在湿滑的赛道上表现出色，途中超越了当地英雄Niki Lauda，为自Sir Jack Brabham退役以来首位赢得比赛的澳大利亚车手。
法拉利车队在1978年对Jones进行了试探，Jones以为他已经达成了协议——然而Enzo 法拉利反悔了，签下了Gilles Villeneuve。Jones最终只得到了来自低级别威廉姆斯车队的报价，车队老板Frank 威廉姆斯和Patrick Head对车队有着宏伟的计划。
Jones几乎驾驶威廉姆斯 FW06赛车在长滩赛道赢得了胜利，但被损坏的机翼阻止了他，然后在布兰兹哈奇赛道，变速箱又出现了问题。在美国大奖赛中，他排在Carlos Reutemann驾驶的法拉利赛车之后，而新的FW07赛车正在Grove完成。
一旦琼斯和他的新队友克莱·雷加佐尼掌握了赛车，他们几乎立刻看起来就像赢家。琼斯在银石赛道领先一大截，直到水泵故障，让瑞士人赢得了车队的第一场胜利。琼斯随后接管了比赛，赢得了剩余六场大奖赛中的四场，最终在锦标赛中排名第三，仅次于乔迪·谢克特和吉尔斯·维伦纽夫。
1980年，琼斯赢得了五场大奖赛——阿根廷、法国、英国、加拿大和美国——从而赢得了世界冠军，并在卡尔德尔的非锦标赛胜利中结束了这一年。
1981年，他又一次表现出色，带领威廉姆斯车队赢得了车队冠军，并在车手冠军的争夺中与纳尔逊·皮克特展开了激烈的竞争。琼斯只赢得了两次胜利，分别在长滩和拉斯维加斯，一系列的未完成比赛和旅行的压力导致他在赛季结束时宣布退役。
他在国内参加了GT赛车和开放式赛车比赛，但回归的渴望太过强烈。1983年，他在长滩赛道驾驶了一辆阿罗尔斯赛车，次年休息了一年，然后在1985年以贝阿特里斯-哈斯车队回归，最初参加了三场大奖赛，然后在1986年完成了整个赛季。他没有再赢得任何比赛，并在赛季结束时退役。
回到澳大利亚，他在后来成为V8 Supercars的比赛中参赛，1995年取得了最佳成绩第二名，甚至还与保时捷和丰田以及Newman-哈斯的CART车队一起参加了赛车运动（包括勒芒）。他在2002年作为迪克·约翰逊赛车队的巴瑟斯特1000公里耐力赛的副驾驶完成了他在职业赛车运动中的最后一次比赛。
在持续的职业赛车运动生涯中，琼斯还取得了成功的媒体生涯，多年来担任澳大利亚一级方程式电视转播的解说员。就像他当时在驾驶舱里一样，他并不害羞，并且直言不讳地表达自己的看法。
琼斯因对赛车运动的贡献于1980年获得了MBE勋章，并于1985年被选入澳大利亚体育名人堂。
他留下了他的妻子和他的六个孩子，克里斯蒂安、艾米伯、扎拉、杰克、卡米拉和艾玛。
detailEn: 1980 F1 world champion Alan Jones dies aged 80

Australia's 1980 Formula 1 world champion Alan Jones has died aged 80 following a short illness, leaving behind a legacy that includes 12 grand prix victories and Williams' first Drivers' Championship title
The 1980 World Drivers’ Champion, Australia’s Alan Jones, died on the Gold Coast on Thursday.
In a statement released on behalf of Jones's family, his wife, Amanda Butler-Davis, said he died following a short illness. He was 80.
“We are extremely saddened to announce the passing of our beloved Alan, who passed away on 5 November following a short illness,” Butler-Davis said.
“He will be dearly missed and fondly remembered by those closest to him, as well as the many fans whose support he was always grateful for.
“Alan dedicated his life to motorsport, building a legacy that will live on through the countless people he touched along the way.
“Through his achievements, passion and unmistakable character, both on and off the track, Alan left an enduring mark on the sport both nationally and across the globe.

“As a family, we would like to take this opportunity to thank everyone who was part of Alan's journey for the many years of friendship, love and support. He was incredibly fortunate to have so many wonderful people around him.”

Jones was born in Melbourne in 1946, the son of businessman and racer Stan Jones, and watched from the sidelines when his father won the 1959 Australian Grand Prix at Longford. The younger Jones repeated the feat at Calder Park in 1980 and remains the last Australian driver to have won the race, which is considered the second-oldest Grand Prix in the world.

Jones dabbled in racing in the UK in the 1960s before returning to Australia, before he moved to London in 1970. It took three years for him to establish himself, winning his first Formula 3 race at Silverstone in 1973, the same year he took second in the British F3 championship in a GRD.
Frank Dernie, Frank Williams and Alan Jones
In 1975 he made his Formula 1 debut at the Spanish Grand Prix, in a Hesketh, and when that team shut at the end of the season he moved to Graham Hill’s team, then to Surtees.

That team also was to close and Jones’s career looked to have stalled – until Shadow called, having lost lead driver Tom Pryce in a tragic crash in South Africa. In a fairytale result, Jones won in Austria, after a brilliant drive on a wet track, passing local hero Niki Lauda on the way to the first win for an Australian since the retirement of Sir Jack Brabham.

Ferrari sounded Jones out for 1978 and Jones thought he had a deal – until Enzo Ferrari reneged, and signed Gilles Villeneuve. Jones was left with an offer from the lowly Williams team, for which owners Frank Williams and Patrick Head had big plans.

Jones nearly took the Williams FW06 to the win at Long Beach, but for a broken wing, then again at Brands Hatch, where a gearbox broke. In the US Grand Prix, he was second to Carlos Reutemann’s Ferrari while a new car, the FW07, was being finished back at Grove.

Once Jones and new team-mate Clay Regazzoni got their hands on the car, they looked like winners nearly immediately. Jones led by a mile at Silverstone until a water pump failed, allowing the Swiss to take the team’s maiden victory. Jones then took over, winning four of the remaining six GPs, to take third in the championship, behind Jody Scheckter and Gilles Villeneuve.
Jones won five grands prix in 1980 — Argentina, France, Britain, Canada and the USA — to claim the world title, topping off the year with the non-championship win at Calder.

In 1981 he again was in fine form, leading Williams to the Constructors’ title and pushing Nelson Piquet hard in the fight for the Drivers’ crown. Jones won only twice, at Long Beach and Las Vegas, and a series of DNFs and the stress of travel led him to announce his retirement at the end of the season.

He raced at home, in GT cars and open-wheelers, but the itch to return was too much. He drove an Arrows at Long Beach in 1983, took the following year off, then returned a year later with the Beatrice-Haas team, first for three GPs and then a full season in 1986. There were no more wins to add to his tally, and he retired at the end of the season.

Back in Australia he raced in what became V8 Supercars, with a best result of second in 1995, and even raced sports cars (including Le Mans) with Porsche and Toyota and CART with Newman-Haas. He made his last start in professional motor racing in 2002, as a Bathurst 1000 co-driver with Dick Johnson Racing.

Alongside his ongoing motorsport career Jones went on to have a successful media career, as a commentator on Australia’s Formula 1 TV coverage, for many years. Just as he was when he was in the cockpit, he was not shy, and called things the way he saw them.
Jones was awarded an MBE for services to motor racing in 1980, and inducted into the Sport Australia Hall of Fame in 1985.
He is survived by his wife and his six children, Christian, Amber, Zara, Jack, Camilla and Emma.

items.originalTitle: 1980 F1 champion Alan Jones passes away
detailZh: 艾伦·琼斯，1980年F1世界冠军，威廉姆斯车队首位世界冠军车手，因短期疾病去世。
本周早些时候，琼斯度过了80岁生日，他曾12次赢得F1赛事。
周四凌晨，琼斯去世的消息传出。
威廉姆斯车队发表声明，表示对琼斯去世深感悲痛。
“艾伦对威廉姆斯车队今天的成就至关重要，他与弗兰克·威廉姆斯和帕特里克·海德建立了非凡的纽带，成为我们参加F1第四个赛季就获得首个车手世界冠军的第一人。”
“他树立了威廉姆斯车队冠军的标准：一个快速、不妥协的赛车手，具有挑战者心态，热爱赛车，并将一生奉献给了这项运动。”
“他是一位真正的澳大利亚偶像，也是威廉姆斯车队的传奇人物，我们将深切地怀念他。”
“我们向琼斯家族和他的所有朋友致以我们的爱和思念。”
detailEn: Alan Jones, the 1980 Formula 1 world champion and first title winner for the Williams F1 team, has passed away after a short illness.
Jones, who turned 80 earlier this week, was a 12-time F1 race winner and the second Australian driver to win the world championship, after Jack Brabham.
News of Jones’s passing emerged during the early hours of Thursday morning.
His former team Williams released a statement saying: “Everyone at Williams is deeply saddened to learn of Alan Jones’ passing.

“Alan was instrumental in making Williams what it is today, forming an extraordinary bond with Frank Williams and Patrick Head to become our first drivers’ world champion in just our fourth season in Formula 1.
“He set the standard for Williams champions: a fast, uncompromising racer with a challenger mentality who loved motor racing and dedicated his life to it.
“He is a true Australian icon and a Williams legend, and he will be dearly missed.
“We send our love and thoughts to the Jones family and all his friends.”

琼斯在F1赛事中赢得了12次胜利。
keyPointsEn: He is the second Australian driver to win the world championship after Jack Brabham.

detailEn: Former Formula 1 world champion Alan Jones dies aged 80
Alan Jones remains the last Australian to win the F1 drivers' championship; he triumphed in 1980 while racing for Williams; Jones won 12 grands prix across his F1 career
Former Formula 1 world champion Alan Jones has died at the age of 80 following a brief illness.
A statement from Jones' family, issued through Motorsport Australia, announced the death of the 1980 championship winner - who remains the last Australian to win the F1 title.

Jones was only the second Australian to win the championship after Sir Jack Brabham, and topped the podium at 12 grands prix during a career that took in spells with Hesketh, Williams - with whom he won his title - and Arrows.
Vale Alan Jones.
It is with great sadness that the Australian Grand Prix Corporation acknowledges the passing of Alan Jones, and we extend our deepest sympathies to his family, loved ones and friends.
As a Formula 1® World Champion and one of Australia’s greatest racing… pic.twitter.com/R79Pkk3rhY
— F1 Australian Grand Prix (@ausgrandprix) November 5, 2026

"We are extremely saddened to announce the passing of our beloved Alan, who passed away on November 5 following a short illness," his wife Amanda Butler-Davis said.
"He will be dearly missed and fondly remembered by those closest to him, as well as the many fans whose support he was always grateful for.
"Alan dedicated his life to motorsport, building a legacy that will live on through the countless people he touched along the way.
"Through his achievements, passion and unmistakable character, both on and off the track, Alan left an enduring mark on the sport both nationally and across the globe.

"As a family, we would like to take this opportunity to thank everyone who was part of Alan's journey for the many years of friendship, love and support. He was incredibly fortunate to have so many wonderful people around him."
Jones is survived by his wife and six children.
